title: Rainy Day Hiring Ladder & Price Stress Simulation
summary: Compact simulation to show how a sequence of hiring ladders (soft freeze, partial pause, hard freeze) combined with stepwise price declines affect runway and unit economics. Built to be shared with GTM/product for alignment on discretionary hiring windows and quick price-recovery triggers.
assumptions: Base monthly burn (payroll+cloud+opex): $4,600k. Baseline ARR growth trajectory unchanged in short-run. Hiring cadence: new-hire ramp to full productivity in 3 months. Average fully-loaded cost per new hire: $20k/month after ramp. Pricing shock applies to hosted API token rates only; embed & dedicated revenue excluded in the initial pass. No layoffs modelled in first 6 months unless scenario explicitly triggers. Cash balance at t0: $120M.

sensitivity_breakdown: Breakdown by line-item: payroll (~70% of burn), cloud (~18%), sales/marketing spend (~8%), misc (~4%). Pricing shock affects revenue recognition, so ARR churn not modelled here but ARPU declines assumed to reduce near-term billing by Price Delta percent on hosted API revenue slice (~35% of revenue mix). Net effect on cash = direct burn savings from paused hires + one-off severance/ops cost (not modelled unless specified).
stepwise_actions: T0: Pause all open IC reqs and delay manager approvals for non-critical roles (0–30 days).
T1: Implement partial hiring band (50%) if shock <20% and cash runway >9 months. Trigger: reconvene finance+GTM weekly.
T2: Full hiring freeze + ops savings target 10% if shock >=25% or runway drop >1.5 months. Trigger: CFO signoff.
T3: Repricing playbook activation: limit new credits, tighten promotional slabs; target +10–20% effective price recovery within 3 months.
T4: If severe and prolonged (>4 months), prepare for role consolidation and headcount rebalancing (scenario for exec review).
quick_notes: 1) Model intentionally conservative on revenue rebound; assumes GTM elasticity lag. 2) Hiring freeze saves are front-loaded (first 2 months) but full savings realized after ramp windows. 3) We should reconcile with Dedicated & Private contract cliffs — this sheet omits long-term contracted revenue cliffs intentionally.
takeaways:
- Small price shocks (<=10%) give limited runway benefit unless paired with disciplined pause on hiring.
- 25–40% price erosion requires a combination of hiring pause + ops savings to meaningfully extend runway (>1.5 months).
- Staggered recovery scenarios show that early, modest pricing actions (coupon reductions, promo cuts) can recover enough ARPU to avoid deeper freezes.
- Recommend pre-authorized hiring-band policy (50% pause automated) once price delta crosses -15% coupled with weekly cadence between Finance & GTM.
